title: Lakebase Search supports Chinese, Japanese, and Korean full-text search
body:
The `lakebase_tokenizer` extension now supports keyword search over Chinese, Japanese, and Korean (CJK) text. These languages don't separate words with spaces, so native PostgreSQL full-text search can't split them into useful search terms. The new `tokenizer_morph` template uses morphological analysis with bundled language dictionaries to segment CJK text into words:

* **Built-in configurations**: installing the extension creates `tokenizer_chinese`, `tokenizer_japanese`, and `tokenizer_korean`. Use them directly with `to_tsvector` without creating a dictionary.
* **Compound handling**: choose a mode that keeps compound words whole, splits them into finer-grained terms, or emits both, depending on the language.
* **Language-aware filtering**: drop Japanese particles and function words, convert Japanese terms to their base form, and filter Korean particles and endings, so matches focus on meaningful terms.

Like `tokenizer_wholeword`, it produces standard `tsvector` values that work with GIN (generalized inverted index) indexes and the `lakebase_text` `lakebase_bm25` index for BM25 (best match 25) ranking. CJK support ships in `lakebase_tokenizer` 0.2.0. If you already use the extension, run `ALTER EXTENSION lakebase_tokenizer UPDATE`. Your existing configurations and indexes don't need to change. See [lakebase\_tokenizer](/aws/en/oltp/projects/lakebase-tokenizer).
